title: Tenant-aware traffic shaper and fallback policies for tiered routing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware traffic shaper that enforces per-tenant quotas and prioritizes requests across Free / Paid / Enterprise tiers, while offering graceful fallback to compatible model variants and alternate regions when capacity or quota constraints occur. The goal is to reduce latency for high-tier customers, protect capacity for enterprise commitments, and keep free-tier users served at degraded quality rather than failing outright. Implementation should be compatible with Smart Routing policies, be configurable via route and tenant metadata, and expose observability hooks in Console for cost/latency attribution.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Initial ticket created by Maya: scope includes traffic shaping algorithm, quota-aware priority levels, fallback model mapping, and console metrics. Marked as P1 due to customer SLA risk during promotional events.

2026-03-11 - Architect review (Rafael): prefer token-budget based shaping over raw request-count to better reflect cost variance between embeddings and generation; suggested API changes to include tenant_priority and tenant_quota metadata on requests.

2026-03-12 - PM feedback (Aisha Patel): add requirement to surface per-tenant denied and downgraded request counts in Console and usage reports; require opt-in for immediate enterprise enforcement during ramp windows.
2026-03-12 - Design note (Ethan Park): UX for tenant-level toggle in Console and an alert when fallback model is being used; small mockups attached in Confluence link.

2026-03-13 - Eng update (Rafael): prototype of shaping policy implemented in feature branch; unit tests for priority queue behavior added. Open question: how to handle persistent KV cache mismatch when switching model variant (decided to invalidate per-tenant cache on variant fallback).

acceptance_criteria: Shaper enforces per-tenant token budgets and applies priority levels: enterprise > paid > free.
When capacity or quota prevents serving at requested model, router chooses a preconfigured fallback model variant and logs the decision with tenant_id and reason.
Requests downgraded due to quota are returned with a structured response field (x-redwood-fallback) and metric emitted for Console.
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant metrics: served_tokens, denied_tokens, downgraded_requests, fallback_model_counts, and average latency by tier.
No regression in overall p95 latency for enterprise-tier traffic under a synthetic mixed workload test.
E2E tests in CI that simulate quota exhaustion and verify correct routing and fallback behavior.
implementation_notes: Add tenant_priority and tenant_token_budget to request metadata; middleware reads from Tenant profile service cache.
Scheduler maintains three priority queues with weights and a configurable smoothing window to avoid starve/revive oscillations.
Quota enforcement uses token accounting; when budget insufficient, try fallback_model_mapping[requested_model] then cross-region fallback if fallback mapping exhausted.
On model-variant fallback, invalidate tenant KV cache for affected session to avoid cache/key mismatch and log a cache_invalidation event.
Expose a decision_reason tag on spans for tracing (quota_exhausted, capacity_throttle, region_unavailable, policy_fallback).
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable shaping for 2% of tenants in us-west-2 only; monitor degraded_requests and enterprise p95 latency.
Stage 2 (regional ramp): expand to 25% of tenants across us-* and eu-* regions; enable console alerts for denied/downgraded rates above threshold.
Stage 3 (global): apply shaping globally and enable enterprise hard-enforcement toggles for tenants with reserved capacity.
Fallback toggles: runtime flags to disable cross-region fallback or model-variant fallback independently for quick rollback.
test_plan: Unit tests for token accounting and priority queue fairness under bursty arrivals.
Integration test: simulate mixed-tier traffic for 30 minutes with quotas and verify no enterprise request is denied when reserved capacity exists.
Chaos test: kill a model serving pool in a region and assert cross-region fallback engages within 200ms and that fallbacks are logged.
Performance test: verify p50/p95 latency targets for enterprise tier remain within SLA with shaping enabled.
